body_es: La economía de la nube transforma fundamentalmente los modelos de gasto en tecnología de información, cambiando desde inversiones de capital (CapEx) hacia gastos operativos (OpEx) más predecibles y controlables. Los clientes eliminan completamente las inversiones upfront significativas en hardware, centros de datos, infraestructura eléctrica y personal especializado en mantenimiento. El modelo flexible de pago por uso de AWS permite que las organizaciones ajusten el gasto según la utilización real, evitando el sobreaprovisionamiento costoso. La elasticidad de la nube permite escalar infraestructura rápidamente durante periodos de demanda alta sin gastos de capital anticipados. AWS proporciona herramientas sofisticadas como AWS Cost Explorer y Trusted Advisor para optimizar y monitorear gastos de forma continua. La reducción de gastos operativos incluye menor necesidad de staff IT dedicado a mantenimiento, eliminación de gastos de aire acondicionamiento y energía, y reducción de costos de desarrollo. El Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) generalmente se reduce significativamente al migrar a AWS.
body_en: Cloud economics fundamentally transforms information technology spending models, shifting from capital investments (CapEx) toward more predictable and controllable operational expenses (OpEx). Customers completely eliminate significant upfront hardware investments, data centers, electrical infrastructure, and specialized maintenance personnel. AWS's flexible pay-as-you-go model allows organizations to adjust spending based on actual utilization, avoiding costly over-provisioning. Cloud elasticity enables rapid infrastructure scaling during high-demand periods without anticipated capital expenses. AWS provides sophisticated tools like AWS Cost Explorer and Trusted Advisor to continuously optimize and monitor spending. Operational expense reduction includes decreased need for dedicated IT maintenance staff, elimination of cooling and electrical costs, and reduced development expenses. Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) is typically significantly reduced when migrating to AWS compared to maintaining infrastructure on-premises. Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) calculations should include all direct and indirect costs of on-premises infrastructure: hardware depreciation, facility costs, power consumption, cooling systems, networking equipment, software licenses, and staffing for maintenance and support. AWS eliminates many of these recurring costs through its shared infrastructure model. Cost optimization becomes an ongoing practice through use of Reserved Instances for predictable workloads, Spot Instances for batch processing, and periodic review using AWS Cost Explorer. Organizations achieving cloud success implement a culture of cost awareness, tagging resources consistently, and regularly reviewing spending against business value delivered. The combination of operational flexibility and cost efficiency makes AWS economically compelling compared to traditional infrastructure approaches.
example_code:
# Get cost and usage data
aws ce get-cost-and-usage   --time-period Start=2024-01-01,End=2024-01-31   --granularity MONTHLY   --metrics BlendedCost   --group-by Type=DIMENSION,Key=SERVICE

# Create a budget alert
aws budgets create-budget   --account-id 123456789012   --budget 'BudgetName=MonthlyLimit,BudgetLimit={Amount=5000,Unit=USD},TimeUnit=MONTHLY'

# Get Reserved Instance recommendations
aws ce get-reservation-purchase-recommendation   --service EC2   --lookback-period THIRTY_DAYS
